title: fleet.result.v1
description: What actually happened when a task ran. Every fact here (SHAs, files changed, acceptance exit codes) is filled in by the orchestrator from things it observed directly -- git, the acceptance commands, the PR API -- never copied from the agent's own account of its work (docs/fleet.md: agents are untrusted narrators). The one field that does carry the agent's own words, agent_report, is explicitly free text and explicitly untrusted.

task_id.description: Id of the fleet/tasks/ task this result belongs to.

status.description: 'succeeded' = acceptance passed and no allowed_paths violation; 'failed' = the agent ran but acceptance or review did not pass; 'rejected' = stopped for touching paths outside allowed_paths or another untrusted-narrator violation; 'blocked' = a need was not satisfied or the kill switch (fleet/STOP) was set before the task could start.

branch.description: Branch the agent actually committed to, observed from git, not copied from the task file.

base_sha.description: SHA the branch was created from, read by the orchestrator at task start.

head_sha.description: SHA of the branch tip, read by the orchestrator at task end.

commits.description: Commits between base_sha and head_sha, as read from git log -- not a count or a summary the agent provided.

files_changed.description: Paths touched between base_sha and head_sha, as read from git diff --name-only.

diff_stat.description: git diff --shortstat between base_sha and head_sha.

allowed_paths_violations.description: Entries of files_changed that matched none of the task's allowed_paths globs. Empty means the agent stayed in bounds; any entry here forces status to 'rejected'.

acceptance_results.description: One entry per acceptance check in the task file, in the same order, run by the orchestrator after the agent hands back control.

agent_report.description: UNTRUSTED. The agent's own free-text account of what it did and why. Useful context for a human or the reviewer, never a substitute for the facts above and never trusted to decide status on its own.

pr.description: The pull request the orchestrator opened for this branch, or null if none has been opened yet (e.g. status is 'blocked' or 'rejected').

reviewer.description: The fresh-context reviewer's verdict (docs/agent-fleet.md section 3.5), or null if review has not run yet.

cost.description: Turns actually used (<= the task's max_turns) and the metered cost of the run.

herdr.description: Optional. Which herdr pane/CLI/worktree actually ran this task, as observed by the orchestrator -- the executed-reality counterpart to the task file's optional 'agent' field (which only states intent). Omitted when the orchestrator does not track pane-level detail for this run.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset.

sha.description: Git object id, abbreviated or full.

name.description: Matches the 'name' of the acceptance check in the task file.

exit_code.description: Actual exit code observed by the orchestrator.

output_tail.description: Last portion of the command's combined output, captured by the orchestrator for triage.

pane.description: Role/pane name the run actually used.

cli.description: Which CLI/model family actually ran this task.

worktree.description: Filesystem path of the worktree the pane ran in, as observed by the orchestrator. Unlike allowed_paths this is a real filesystem location (often absolute), not a repo-relative glob.

session_id.description: Opaque session/log identifier for that pane run, if the CLI exposes one.
